text:
sara: Heads-up — noticed org `team-x` hit burst caps for the large-3B family and trafficked into the fallback 1.3B model for ~4m. We got an uptick from a campaign. Need quick triage: why did fallback happen so aggressively and how do we show better signals in the console?
ben: thanks, saw the same in logs. quota engine emitted `RATE_LIMIT_BURST_EXCEEDED` and routing selected fallback per policy.
carla: can you paste the request headers/route id? curious if the request used `prefer_low_latency=true` which can force family fallback.
sara: here's sanitized header from the sample: ```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer xxxxx
X-Redwood-Model-Family: redwood-3b
X-Redwood-Prefer: low_latency
X-Redwood-Client-Org: team-x
```
emma: console currently shows "fallback applied" only as an event in the timeline, not per-request breakdown. we should surface the fallback reason (quota vs capacity) in the trace view. :eyes:
ben: agree. two questions: 1) do we want the quota subsystem to emit a `fallback_reason` tag (quota|capacity|policy) on the routing decision? 2) do we expose it in metrics as a label for per-model-family counters?
jorge: +1 to both. for telemetry we need a label so we can graph "fallback_rate by model_family". otherwise ops can't tell if it's a quota issue or model OOM.
carla: telemetry OK, but careful about cardinality. model_family and fallback_reason are fine. do not attach request_id or client payload.
sara: also saw surprising behavior: the client hit a burst allowance (credits) that should have lasted 10m but got consumed quickly because of interactive short calls with small responses. maybe our burst window calculation skews for low-token requests.
ben: that rings a bell — our credit spend estimator uses tokens *per-request* not token-rate. short requests cause more frequent credit deductions. quick patch idea: amortize credits per-second over a sliding window instead of per-call decrement.
emma: UX ask — add an entry in quota debugging panel: "recent fallback events" with columns: time, org, model_family, reason, pre_quota_balance. clickable to jump to request trace.
carla: ops-bot can we add an alert rule: if fallback_rate(model_family=redwood-3b) > 0.05 for 5m, create incident-channel notification (but not pager)?
ops-bot: rule created: fallback_rate(redwood-3b) > 0.05 for 5m -> post to #incidents-ops (no page). ID: FBR-2026-1207.
ben: I'll prototype the `fallback_reason` tag in the routing layer today and add Prometheus label. will also open a PR for amortized burst deduction — might be a config toggle so we can A/B.
sara: nice. can someone own the console piece? emma? we need to show per-model-family quota balance and recent fallback events in the quota tab.
emma: I can take it. will mock a panel and flag it behind feature flag `quota_fallback_insights`. mockups by EOD tomorrow.
jorge: I'll add Grafana dashboard: fallback_rate by family + moving avg of pre_quota_balance. useful to correlate with campaigns.
carla: follow-ups: (1) add tests for credit amortization edge cases, (2) ensure telemetry doesn't include PII, (3) docs for Support on new console fields.
sara: created GH issue: redwood/repo#4521 — "Model-family fallback visibility + amortized burst credits". assigning: ben (routing + quotas), emma (console), jorge (dash/metrics), carla (telemetry & tests). ETA runbook + small rollback plan by next Tue.
ben: pinging @eng-oncall if we need fast rollback.
sara: thanks all. saving traces and sampling raw requests for the spike to the incident attach. :white_check_mark:
emma: will add a small UI note: "fallback shown when routing replaces requested model" and link to docs.
carla: one more: we should include the effective capacity tier in the per-request trace (hosted/dedicated/private) so Support can tell when a fallback was due to capacity tier constraints.
ben: good call. will include `capacity_tier` in the routing envelope.
ops-bot: incident-attach saved to ticket: INC-2026-88.
sara: cool. closing thread for now — will post updates in the GH issue. :rocket:
